summary: Preserved the candidate's valid NPU MoE reload regression and corrected its overbroad GPU identity evidence: this prepared review is MI350X according to both PyTorch and rocm-smi, while gfx950 alone does not distinguish the marketed model across environments. No additional production source correction was justified because the prepared base already contains the canonical-layout fix.

tests.what_was_measured: Before changing the candidate, all three focused post-process and separate-expert reload regressions passed.
PyTorch and rocm-smi independently identified the single assigned GPU as AMD Instinct MI350X; PyTorch reported gfx950:sramecc+:xnack- and rocm-smi reported gfx950.
After consolidating the evidence correction, the same three focused regressions passed.

gpu_execution.evidence: reports/j-b768c099c947/raw/device_identity.txt records direct PyTorch and rocm-smi identity queries on the assigned MI350X. The GPU was used for identity evidence; no Ascend kernel execution is claimed.

remaining_limitations: No Ascend device, CANN, or torch_npu runtime was available, so actual npu_format_cast and Ascend grouped-matmul behavior were not independently executed.
The reported DeepSeekV3.2 weights were unavailable, so no full Engine or HTTP update_weights_from_disk run established scheduler survival after reload.
The focused regression mocks NPU format casting and validates loader layout only; it does not qualify NPU kernels, model semantics, HTTP transport, scheduler survival, or distributed execution.
